claims.claim: Amazon-to-Taobao/JD cross-platform comparison was actually implemented by PriceDoge by 2019.
claims.counterevidence: PriceDoge described title-based similar-product search rather than guaranteed exact-SKU identity resolution, and its public GitHub footprint is small.

claims.claim: By 2026 multiple public tools implement substantial portions of Amazon-to-China sourcing, including Amazon-to-1688 matching and in some cases landed-cost estimation.
claims.counterevidence: The closest 2026 Chrome extensions observed have very small public user counts and are primarily seller/importer tools rather than mainstream consumer routers.

claims.claim: Product identity, dynamic price state, authentication, CAPTCHA, rate limiting and source-platform access are recurring technical frictions, but authorized/API-based access can mitigate at least some of them.
claims.counterevidence: Baopals states that some shop and product information is supplied via e-commerce-platform APIs, so platform access should not be characterized as universally impossible.

claims.claim: A scaled buying-agent business can suffer severe operational disruption from source-platform counterparty actions; ezbuy experienced large-scale Taobao account and warehouse-address restrictions in 2017.
claims.counterevidence: Ezbuy had millions of customers and was subsequently acquired; the incident therefore does not establish that the agent model itself is commercially nonviable.

claims.claim: Consumer proxy-purchasing and forwarding infrastructure already exists at meaningful scale, so absence of forwarding infrastructure alone does not explain the missing neutral router.
claims.counterevidence: Existing agents optimize their own procurement/forwarding workflows rather than proving that a channel-neutral U.S.-consumer comparison layer is economically attractive.

claims.claim: Browser-extension distribution is not by itself a structural reason a shopping-assistance product cannot reach mass scale.
claims.counterevidence: Honey's merchant and affiliate economics differ substantially from a China-direct neutral routing product.

claims.claim: Security and litigation exposure are real risks for proxy-shopping platforms, but available court evidence does not establish that a passive facilitator is necessarily treated like the underlying seller or manufacturer.
claims.counterevidence: Pandabuy-related proceedings and default issues show continuing legal exposure, while prior judicial analysis cited in related litigation cut against an automatic seller-equivalence theory.

claims.claim: Commercialization is currently fragmented across consumer agents, seller sourcing tools, dropshipping automation and agent interoperability rather than concentrated in one neutral U.S.-consumer routing layer.
claims.counterevidence: Bounded public-web research cannot rule out private, stealth, mobile-only or poorly indexed integrated competitors.

claims.claim: The closest publicly visible 2026 tools suggest that landed-cost computation itself is implementable; the unresolved scaling problem appears to be integration of reliable identity, data state, execution, platform access and consumer distribution.
claims.counterevidence: The observed products are tiny or seller-focused, so their existence does not prove the same architecture works economically for ordinary U.S. consumers.

claims.claim: A neutrality-versus-affiliate or merchant-funded monetization conflict may help explain why sourcing/comparison products cluster around sellers and affiliate workflows rather than neutral consumer routing.
claims.counterevidence: No identified failed company directly attributed its failure to this incentive conflict; alternative explanations such as data reliability, operations or insufficient consumer demand remain viable.

data_gaps.gap: Current authenticated access behavior for Taobao, Tmall, JD and related ranking/search endpoints was not tested.
No paid venture/startup database was accessed, so stealth or discontinued companies may be missing.
Wegobuy could not be reliably opened in this session; third-party legacy labels are insufficient to establish current corporate status.
Sugargoo, CSSBuy and CNFans public sites were reachable but this bounded session did not obtain sufficiently auditable primary history or scale data to make material claims about them.
No Chrome extension install-history time series was available; reported user counts are retrieval-time snapshots only.
No founder interviews, direct company contacts, purchases, quotations or paid datasets were used.
Public evidence does not establish causal consumer acquisition economics for a neutral U.S.-to-China routing product.
